label: Essential-state event and prior…: An event is a change from one state of affairs to another with…
term: essential-state event and prior explanatory cause (survey A3)
definition: An event is a change from one state of affairs to another with those states essential to its identity. A3P1 describes a cause as a prior condition capable of explaining or partly explaining an event; A3C describes a prior condition that explains or partly explains something else. Possible causability of the SAME event must preserve its essential states. Neither wording alone defines a concrete individual bearer, temporal presence or complete explanatory sufficiency.
note: Owner approved exploring BOTH state-pair sufficiency and distinct occurrence interpretations (2026-11-09). TruthCore.Causality.EventIdentityProfiles supplies separate unrestricted analyst types with structured contents and a bearer/ordered-interval occurrence criterion. These are alternatives, not a faithful mapping of the original A3 sense. Matching contents support possible conditioning of the pair; conditioning of the SAME selected occurrence additionally requires local occurrence uniqueness. The repeated-transition control refutes that inference without uniqueness. Concrete bearer, real temporal presence, explanatory priority, firstness, contingency exclusion and modal actuality dictionaries remain OPEN. No original allowance removed; no renewed owner fork needed.
